prize_parts.citation: For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases by engineered deaminases without double-strand cleavage.

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from nitrogenase (B012) to base editing (B062) as a single-part prize. The round-1 exchange tested my own first choice and I do not think it survives. Linke, Zou and I all place the open catalytic mechanism (the E4 hydride state, the N2 binding site) at the centre of the problem, and a citation limited to structure would not be the mechanism prize I argued for. Five credited names against a three-person limit, with Dean and Ribbe equally decisive on genetics and cofactor assembly, make the cut hard to defend, and no other member moved toward B012. Base editing is the candidate that best meets the test I actually apply, a chemical mechanism converted into a controllable capability. A deaminase is tethered to a programmable DNA-binding protein so that one base is converted to another without a double-strand break. The adenine editor required directed evolution of a deaminase that had no known activity on DNA, which is enzyme chemistry and not only fusion engineering. The result has been reproduced by many independent laboratories, its editing outcomes are well characterised, and clinical use has begun. With a single part, three names fit without leaving the discovery incomplete: Liu conceived and directed the programme, Komor made the first cytosine base editor, and Gaudelli made the first adenine base editor. Chabes and Zou proposed this set at opening, and Linke and Somfai both said they would accept it if the prize has one part.
statement.case_against: Base editing is only about ten years old and clinical outcomes are still accumulating, so some of the weight rests on tool impact. The independent Kondo and Nishida deaminase-fusion work is a real competing claim, and my three names do not resolve it. Rewarding the genome-editing area so soon after the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize may read as an extension of recognised work. Naming two former trainees alongside the group leader departs from Aqvist's and Somfai's view that Liu alone is the defensible attribution. A one-part prize also leaves out the mature synthetic and mechanistic chemistry (B039, B015) that several members value. The central evidence on dated priority is not in the files I may read, and I am working from memory of the 2016 and 2017 papers.

responses.point: Aqvist proposes Liu alone for base editing, paired with Crews and Handa for degradation, arguing that trainees should not use up slots a second achievement needs.
responses.response: I accept that a Liu-alone citation is defensible when the three-person limit has to carry a second achievement, and I can see why you built the pairing. My difficulty is that you also say you would reconsider Komor and Gaudelli if base editing is the sole part, and I think that is the likelier outcome. Your own round-1 text calls Gaudelli's TadA evolution real chemistry rather than routine work, and I rely on exactly that point. I also doubt the second part can be made clean within the limit: you credit Crews and Handa while naming Deshaies and Ciulli as decisive, so you leave out two contributors you regard as decisive. I would rather give the three names to the one achievement whose first demonstrations are tied to specific experiments.

responses.point: Linke prefers Pd-catalysed C-N coupling plus Liu alone, and says that if the committee wants a single-achievement prize he would support Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as the defensible set. He also judged my nitrogenase case: the structure is mature, the mechanism is not closed, and no citation is both fair and accurate.
responses.response: I accept the nitrogenase criticism. That is the main reason I moved. On your configuration, I take the C-N case seriously: the attribution is the cleanest on the list and the catalytic cycle is well understood. But you concede that nothing links the two parts, and you say B039 may look derivative after 2010. I put the question I asked in round 1 and still cannot answer from the files I may read: the ligand-design advance has to stand as a distinct principle. A two-part prize also forces Liu alone, which leaves out the experimental first authors. Since you have said you would back Liu, Komor and Gaudelli for a one-part prize, I ask you to treat that as your fallback now. I keep B039 as my second alternative and would not oppose it.

responses.point: Zou criticises my nitrogenase proposal: the structure is secure, but where N2 binds and what the E4 state is remain open, so a citation would overstate what was shown. Zou also says the Komor-Gaudelli work and the independent Kondo and Nishida claim need explicit treatment.
responses.response: You are right on the first point, and I agree with the reasoning you gave for ranking B012 sixth. A citation for the structure would have been honest but would not have been a mechanism prize. I credit your second point as the strongest objection to my new position. The citation has to say explicitly what the committee decided about Kondo and Nishida. My answer is that the claim is a genuine independent demonstration of a cytidine deaminase fusion, but the programme that produced both editor classes, with the directed-evolved adenine editor, is Liu's, and a three-name limit forces a choice. I hold that as a judgement and not as a finding, and I would welcome the expert report on the dating if the committee has one. Your own ranking of B062 third and your listing of it as an alternative make it the one candidate where we may be close.

responses.point: Chabes values a defined chemical reaction made programmable, singles out the evolved TadA deaminase as real enzyme chemistry, and moved in his round-1 file to Liu alone only to answer Aqvist, while keeping Liu, Komor and Gaudelli in his opening and response text.
responses.response: I agree with your reading of the adenine editor, and it is the main reason I now support B062. I would prefer that your file state the set you really hold. If B062 is the only part, as I now propose, the trio is the one you originally proposed, and it avoids the problem you note of a prize that credits only a laboratory head. On B066 you say you would be comfortable with it, and I keep it as my first alternative because the cereblon-mediated glue mechanism is the part I find easiest to defend mechanistically. I do not share your confidence that base editing is better as a single chemical idea than degradation on maturity, since neither has an approved bifunctional or editing drug at scale, but I judge the first-demonstration evidence to be sharper for base editing.

responses.point: Somfai supports Liu alone as the second part of a two-part prize with Buchwald and Hartwig, says Komor and Gaudelli are essential trainees, and says he would reconsider only if the committee drops the second part.
responses.response: That is the condition I am proposing: one part. You also said base editing alone does not make a chemistry prize for you because it would leave out a core synthetic method. I take the point about balance, but I do not think a prize must span subfields, and I would not put a part into the configuration purely for breadth. You are right that Buchwald and Hartwig are the decisive pair for the general amine method and that Kosugi is a precursor. I can accept that part's attribution but I still want the distinction from the 2010 prize put in the citation if the committee takes up B039.

responses.point: Aili ranks targeted protein degradation first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and concedes that the three-person cut is contestable and that no bifunctional degrader is approved.
responses.response: I considered moving to B066 and I still rate it the strongest candidate that is not mine. My hesitation is the one you name. PROTACs and cereblon-based glues rest on different discoveries, and three members have given three different trios. Handa's cereblon work is the easiest part to defend; the PROTAC half is disputed between Crews and Deshaies on one side and Ciulli and Gray on the other. I do not think the committee can write a single citation that is accurate for both. If the committee settles on the trio and a citation that splits them honestly, I would support it, but at present I judge B062 to have the cleaner first-demonstration record.

uncertainties: Whether the dated primary record separates the Komor and Gaudelli first demonstrations from Kondo and Nishida's deaminase fusion clearly enough to omit the latter. I am working from memory and have not seen the expert report on attribution.
Whether the committee will accept three names (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) in a one-part prize when two members prefer Liu alone for a two-part prize.
Whether base editing is mature enough at ten years, given that long-term clinical durability and safety data are still accumulating.
Whether the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize makes this read as an extension of genome editing instead of a distinct chemical principle.
statement.conflict_note: No personal, collaborative or institutional conflict with any credited candidate in B062, B066 or B039. My own field (respiratory enzymes, proton and electron transfer) is no longer relevant to my preferred part, since I have withdrawn B012, and I do not think it biases me toward base editing. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, whose first choice is B033; that does not affect my configuration. As Secretary I am responsible for process and the expert reports, and I try to keep that separate from my scientific view.
